description: Use this when the user wants a genogram or family diagram with standard symbols drawn from people and their relationships, for example "draw a genogram of my family" or "make a three-generation genogram for my social work class". Takes people (id, name, sex, birth and death years, deceased, index person; no label or notes), relations (couple: married, divorced, separated, cohabiting, engaged; parent_child: biological, adopted, foster; twins: identical, fraternal; emotional: close, distant, conflict, cut_off, hostile), an optional household, a title and a page size. Returns counts, each person's generation number, a geometry check (overlapping symbols or names, family lines through a name), the legend of symbols used, an interactive chart, and PDF, SVG, people CSV and relationships CSV downloads. An emotional relationship is drawn as a line only between two people next to each other in the same row; all others, including any between a parent and a child, are listed in a "Relationships not drawn" table and are not in the legend. Refuses unknown ids, parent cycles, more than 2 biological parents and impossible years, naming the problem. Up to 150 people, 12 generations and 100 emotional relationships. Relationships only: does not take health or medical details. Download links of large charts expire after about 1 hour.

household.description: Ids of the people who live together; drawn with a dashed outline, e.g. ["p2","p3"].

page_size.description: PDF page: letter (default), a4, tabloid, a3 or a2. One page when the whole chart fits with text of at least 6 pt; else the chart prints in overlapping parts at full size.

death_year.description: 4-digit death year, e.g. 2019. Marks the person as deceased.

deceased.description: true draws an X through the symbol when the death year is not known.

id.description: Short unique id, up to 40 characters, used in relations, e.g. "p1" or "maria".

index.description: true for the index person (the person the genogram is about); drawn with a double line. At most one.

name.description: Name shown under the symbol, up to 60 characters, e.g. "Maria Kowalska".

sex.description: M (square), F (circle), X (diamond) or unknown (diamond with ?). Default unknown.

relations.description: The relationships, up to 600 (at most 150 couples and 100 emotional). Example: [{"type":"couple","a":"p1","b":"p2","kind":"married","start_year":1975},{"type":"parent_child","a":"p1","b":"p3"},{"type":"parent_child","a":"p2","b":"p3"}].

a.description: Person id. For parent_child this is the parent, e.g. "p1".

b.description: Person id. For parent_child this is the child, e.g. "p3".

end_year.description: Year a couple divorced, separated or ended, e.g. 1995.

kind.description: couple: married (default), divorced, separated, cohabiting, engaged. parent_child: biological (default), adopted, foster. twins: identical, fraternal (default). emotional: close (default), distant, conflict, cut_off, hostile.

start_year.description: Year a couple married or began, e.g. 1981.

type.description: couple, parent_child (a is the parent, b the child), twins, or emotional.

title.description: Title printed on the chart and used in file names, up to 80 characters, e.g. "Kowalski family".
